audit_findings.title: Historical owner earnings span incompatible business perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: $474.1m (38.5%) gap between supplied 2023 OE of $1,230.1m and a $756.0m continuing-operations proxy computed as $408.4m net earnings plus $426.2m depreciation and amortization less $78.6m capex; exact rebuilt OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The inconsistent historical series affects the trend anchor, growth assumptions, and too-hard judgment; under the MIN(trend, latest) rule, a rebuilt trend below $853.2m would also reduce anchor OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For example, in 2018, we split-off most of our automation and specialty platform in a Reverse Morris Trust transaction with Altra Industrial Motion Corp. and, in 2020 and 2025, we spun-off our former Industrial Technologies segment and our former Precision Technologies segment, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated comparability error, not merely a possible issue. The 2025 filing recasts 2023-2025 for discontinued Ralliant operations, while the supplied 2023 OE is far above a continuing-operations proxy. Rebuilding the series could lower the trend anchor, but the cleaner post-separation trajectory could also support a less pessimistic growth judgment, so the net value direction is mixed.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2016-2025 OE on Fortive's current continuing-operations perimeter using identical OE adjustments for every year, document each separation adjustment, and rerun the trend anchor, growth cases, too-hard flag, and valuation.

audit_findings.title: Large intangible-amortization add-back may omit required reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $368m of 2025 amortization, equal to 43.1% of the $853.2m OE anchor; recurring replacement requirement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring spending needed to maintain acquired technology, customer relationships, software, or brands must reduce OE or the sustainable growth supported by OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Total intangible amortization expense in 2025, 2024, and 2023 was $ 368 million, $ 369 million and $ 367 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The large add-back is demonstrated, but an omitted maintenance requirement is not. Some economic replacement spending may already be expensed through R&D or SG&A, while acquisition accounting amortization may be non-economic. Nevertheless, the gross exposure is large enough that even a minority judged to require incremental reinvestment could materially change intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $368m by asset class and acquisition, identify maintenance spending already captured in R&D, SG&A, capitalized software, capex, and acquisitions, then rerun OE after deducting only the evidenced recurring replacement amount.

audit_findings.title: FY2024 was available but omitted from the judged series
audit_findings.magnitude: $827.3m continuing-operations proxy computed as $482.5m net earnings plus $430.9m depreciation and amortization less $86.1m capex; $25.9m or 3.0% below the $853.2m anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The omitted year affects the historical trend, perimeter assessment, growth judgment, and too-hard rationale, although the latest-year anchor is unchanged directly.
audit_findings.evidence: The following discussion and analysis of Fortive’s financial condition and results of operations for the fiscal years ended December 31, 2025, December 31, 2024, and December 31, 2023 should be read in conjunction with our audited consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes included in Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated. On filed components, 2024 appears close to 2025 rather than supporting a 31% operating collapse. Its direct scale is only 3.0% below the anchor, but the record does not establish how the exact OE adjustments or corrected trajectory would change the selected growth cases, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Calculate FY2024 OE using exactly the same adjustments applied to FY2025, insert it into the current-perimeter series, and rerun the trend, growth, perimeter, and too-hard judgments.

audit_findings.title: Separation indemnities are an unmodeled senior contingent claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A realized indemnity would be a cash claim ahead of common equity, entering as a bridge deduction or as a nonrecurring reduction in future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: If we are required to indemnify Vontier or Ralliant under the circumstances set forth in these agreements, we may be subject to substantial liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The agreements and contingent obligations exist, but the supplied record demonstrates no asserted claim, probable loss, or estimable exposure. The 2025 filing reports immaterial self-insurance and litigation accruals and the latest 10-Q reports no material risk-factor change. This is therefore a forward-looking contingency rather than a demonstrated valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Review the separation and tax-matters agreements, current claims correspondence, accruals, reasonably possible loss ranges, insurance, and reciprocal indemnities; rerun the bridge if a claim becomes probable or an exposure becomes estimable.

audit_findings.title: The OE anchor embeds an unusually low tax burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $57.0m annual tax difference between the filed $69.5m provision and 21% of $602.2m pretax earnings; approximately $2.54 per base-case share and $3.00 per bull-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: A higher sustainable tax rate reduces post-tax OE and therefore operating PV across all scenarios.
audit_findings.evidence: Our effective tax rate was 11.5%, 4.7%, 5.7% during 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The 11.5% reported rate is demonstrated, but its unsustainability is not: the filing identifies foreign-derived income deductions, foreign tax effects, credits, and uncertain-tax-position changes. As a scale test, normalizing fully to the filed 21% federal benchmark would reduce base value from $39.19 to about $36.65 and bull value from $46.03 to about $43.03. Both remain well below the $56.94 price, so this benchmark cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Separate structural deductions and credits from discrete benefits and determine a sustainable cash tax rate; rerun OE only if that evidence implies a recurring burden materially different from the rate embedded in the anchor.

audit_findings.title: All reported cash is treated as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $374.2m, equal to $1.19 per diluted share and 3.0% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Required, restricted, trapped, or tax-burdened cash should be excluded from the equity bridge rather than added as distributable excess cash.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we held approximately $376 million of cash and cash equivalents that were invested in highly liquid investment-grade instruments with a maturity of 90 days or less, of which approximately 80% was held outside of the United States.
audit_findings.explanation: The entire $374.2m bridge addition is exposed, while the latest filing states that 91% is held outside the United States. Even removing all cash would reduce base value only from $39.19 to about $38.00 and bull value from $46.03 to about $44.84, still $12.10 below the $56.94 market price. The actual unavailable portion must be smaller than this full-removal test, so it cannot change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Determine minimum operating cash, restrictions, geographic location, and remittance costs, then replace the bridge addition with verified distributable cash in the next valuation update.
